clue.text: Elderly muddler in railway museum?

definitions.meaning: a fussy, slightly incompetent old man, in British slang
a buffer from the railways, of the kind kept as an exhibit, would be an aged one

explanation.walkthrough: A buffer is the sprung stop at the end of a railway track or on a carriage; an old one belongs in a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a bumbling, old-fashioned man a buffer, so an aged bumbler is the old sort.

clue.text: A harp gone astray at home for the bereaved

indicators.note: letters going astray wander off from their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harp has wandered off from a house for those in mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution housing children who have lost their parents.

clue.text: Game that might turn into a fiddle?

definitions.text: Game that might turn into a fiddle?

parts.words: Game that might turn into a fiddle?
parts.note: a pub game whose name, rearranged, gives the short name for a Stradivarius violin

explanation.walkthrough: The game's five letters rearranged spell STRAD, short for a Stradivarius violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub game of throwing at a board whose letters can become a violin's name.

clue.text: Creation of single lines ?

parts.note: uni- is the prefix meaning single or one
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A poet describes a work consisting of a single line.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything that was created, the whole cosmos.

clue.text: Girl has a wild life on the town

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A young woman enjoys a riotous night out in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' is the definition, a given name; 'wild' is the anagram signal, and 'on' sets the jumbled piece ahead of the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, also meaning happiness.

clue.text: Haphazard artist gets point on Benedictine style

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
N, north, is a point of the compass
Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A careless painter picks up the manner of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Without plan or pattern, by chance.

clue.text: Kipling's African marchers

parts.note: Kipling's poem about soldiers in the Boer War repeats the footwear 'moving up and down again' as they tramp across Africa

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem of that title has its refrain about infantry footwear 'slog-slog-slogging over Africa'.
explanation.definitionFit: The marching things in Kipling's Boer War poem are soldiers' footwear, which gives the poem its title.

clue.text: Are the Archers cockneys ?

parts.note: archers are men with bows, and cockneys are men born within sound of Bow Bells in London

explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of East London; The Archers is also a long-running BBC radio soap about country folk, which is the misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers shoot with bows; men from London's Bow district would share the name.

clue.text: Surgeons working an exchange system?

definitions.meaning: doctors who carry out operations
staff connecting calls at a telephone exchange

explanation.definitionFit: Both those who cut patients open in theatre and those who once connected telephone calls at a switchboard.

clue.text: For an old sailor this is the form to back

definitions.text: For an old sailor this is the form to back

parts.words: For an old sailor this is the form to back
parts.note: a veteran seaman is called a word made of this hard casing plus 'back'

explanation.walkthrough: An old salt is nicknamed a 'shellback', so this word put before 'back' gives the term.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard outer casing, or form, which with 'back' added makes the nickname of a veteran seaman.

clue.text: It's not fair to turn over Trap One to Scarface

indicators.note: turning a word over makes it read in the opposite direction, so trap is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
the Roman numeral for one is I
Scarface was the nickname of the gangster Al Capone

explanation.surface: A greyhound-racing complaint: trap one was unfairly handed over to a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' turns TRAP into PART; Scarface was Al Capone's nickname, giving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased judgment favours one side, which is why it is not fair.

clue.text: First edition of Erewhon is not in place

indicators.note: the earliest version of the title, before Butler rearranged it, means its letters are shuffled back into order

explanation.surface: A book collector notes the first printing of Samuel Butler's novel is missing from its shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Butler named his imaginary land Erewhon by roughly turning a word round; 'First edition of' asks for that original word, an anagram of EREWHON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in no place at all is not to be found anywhere.

clue.text: There's division in the Church, I'll say

indicators.note: say tells us the word I'll is to be spoken out loud and matched by its sound

parts.note: the contraction of 'I will', pronounced like the passage between pews

explanation.surface: Someone declares there's a split among churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: The passage between rows of pews divides a church's seating into parts.

clue.text: It might have been fatal to ring off

definitions.meaning: a narrow escape from disaster
to end a telephone conversation

explanation.walkthrough: 'ring off' is British for putting the phone down, which shuts a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss nearly killed someone; ending a phone conversation is shutting it, read literally.

clue.text: Fitting as a quiet river location

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A quiet riverside spot is described as just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting and pertinent remarks are both apt to the occasion.

clue.text: Baltic dogs' home

parts.note: a region on the Baltic coast that gave its name to a small fluffy breed of dog

explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic region from which the small fluffy lapdog breed takes its name.

clue.text: Old bird calls for action

definitions.meaning: the extinct flightless bird of Mauritius
the imperative 'do!' said twice, urging someone to act

explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless bird of Mauritius, and also two cries of 'do!' urging action.

clue.text: No bull-ring has a doctor, by the way ; that's the ultimate position

parts.note: on a dartboard or target, the ring outside the bull's-eye is the outer
MO, medical officer, is a doctor
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A bullfight with no arena has a doctor standing by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' is the target's centre, not a bullfight; the ring just around it is called the outer.
explanation.definitionFit: Furthest from the centre, at the very edge.

clue.text: Having two pairs, call it a game!

definitions.text: Having two pairs, call it a game!

parts.words: Having two pairs, call it a game!
parts.note: a golf match played by two sides of two players each

explanation.definitionFit: A golf match with two partnerships, a group of four in all.

clue.text: Made out Desmond was in tears

parts.note: Des is short for Desmond
cried means was in tears

explanation.definitionFit: To discern or catch sight of something at a distance.

clue.text: Jane's heroine named by letter

definitions.meaning: the title character of a Jane Austen novel
in the old signalling alphabet M was spoken as this name

explanation.walkthrough: Old British military signallers used this girl's name for the letter M, as in 'pip emma' for p.m.
explanation.definitionFit: Austen's novel takes its heroine's name for its title; old signallers' code used the same name for the letter M.

clue.text: Where to find a bit of uneasy rest

parts.note: some means a bit of, a certain amount

indicators.note: uneasy suggests restless disorder, so the letters of rest are jumbled

explanation.surface: A restless sleeper asks where a little troubled repose might be had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasy' is the anagram signal on rest. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England, so it answers 'Where'.
explanation.definitionFit: A place in south-west England, so it answers 'where'.

clue.text: Deserts me ? Right, it's the end

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned asks whether this is how it all ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' is the noun, as in 'just deserts', not the verb meaning abandons.
explanation.definitionFit: What one deserves, good or bad, as in just deserts.

clue.text: Dramatically produces coaches

definitions.meaning: puts on a play in a theatre
horse-drawn coaches running in ... along a route

explanation.definitionFit: Puts on a play, and the old horse-drawn coaches that ran a route in sections.

clue.text: Bellicose juggler

definitions.meaning: aggressive and eager for a fight
a street performer or entertainer who swallows flames

explanation.definitionFit: A hothead spoiling for a fight, and a circus performer who swallows flames like a juggler does tricks.

clue.text: Controllers of life's thread

parts.note: the three goddesses of Greek myth who spin, measure and cut each mortal's thread of life

explanation.definitionFit: The three goddesses of myth who spin, measure and cut every mortal's thread of life.

clue.text: Disguise is about finished

parts.note: C, for circa, is the abbreviation for about
over means finished

explanation.surface: A masquerade is said to be at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A false identity masks the real one, as a disguise does.

clue.text: Playgirl found in bed, all strung up

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Shakespeare's play Twelfth Night

definitions.text: found in bed, all strung up
definitions.meaning: a pansy-like flower in a garden bed, and a stringed instrument

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Twelfth Night heroine, a garden pansy, and a string instrument a little larger than a violin.

clue.text: Hiding from the effect of the sun

definitions.meaning: a thrashing or beating
skin turning brown in sunlight

explanation.definitionFit: A beating, and browning skin in sunlight; both also name curing animal hides into leather.

clue.text: Exotic flower from private in love with colonel

parts.note: OR, other ranks, covers privates in the army
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
CO, commanding officer, is often a colonel

explanation.surface: An exotic bloom is obtained from a soldier who is in love with his colonel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: a river, here the great South American one.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, and this one in Venezuela is far from Britain.

clue.text: Remains of old female garment

definitions.meaning: continues to stay put
a laced corset worn by women in former times

explanation.definitionFit: To linger means to stay put; a whalebone corset was formerly called this.

clue.text: Firm gets dates wrong before Lent

indicators.note: getting the dates wrong suggests jumbling them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting, a fast

explanation.surface: A company mixes up its diary in the run-up to Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram signal on dates, and 'before' places that result ahead of the Lenten abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwavering and resolute, as in a firm friend.
